sessions.lever: Group B: ALLOCDBG table via a new generic single-function isolator; accumulator-signedness and big_size-staging probes
sessions.note: NO MOVEMENT; Group B is a plateau at 30 and the numbers say why. NEW INSTRUMENT: tmp/ce0c_allocone.sh isolates func_8007CE0C into its own TU (tmp/allocone.sh is hardcoded to hirahira_w_ctrl). Verified faithful - the isolated compile reports `.frame $sp,80 vars=32`, identical to the in-context measurement - so allocno numbering, nrefs, livelen and pri can be read without block-alignment guesswork. OUR CALLEE-SAVED ALLOCATION (pseudo, nrefs/livelen/pri): s0<-p78 (10/39/7692), s1<-p72 (8/70/3428), s2<-p73 (8/89/2696), s3<-p118 (3/14/2142), s4<-p77 (4/52/1538), s5<-p74 (2/120/166). Target holds big_size in s0 (`sra s0,v1,0x5`) and copies it through v1 into s4; we hold it in s4 = p77 at pri 1538. THE SIZING VERDICT: to move big_size into s0 its allocno must outrank p78 at 7692, i.e. a ~5x lift - NOT a narrow tie like hirahira_w_ctrl's 0.4-15% gaps, where a single extra reference or one insn of live range flipped the order. A 5x lift needs either many more references or a live range cut from 52 to about 10, neither of which any natural spelling supplies. That is a materially different regime and should be stated as such rather than ground at blindly. ROUND-9 PROBES ALL HOLD AT 30 (143 insns, frame 80 throughout): x accumulator s16 instead of u16 (30 - same score, and note candidate-30's u16 is what makes cc1 emit `lhu` for the x load where target has `lh`); y accumulator a0_tmp u16->s16 (36, worse - it is load-bearing as u16); both narrowed (36); big_size staged through a second variable to mirror target's move v1,s0 / move s4,v1 pair (30); x_s16 plus big staging (30). src/display.c reverted.

sessions.lever: Group B sizing: derive target's implied allocation order, list inversions, compute deltas
sessions.note: ENDGAME STATEMENT FOR GROUP B - and the sizing shows the PRIORITY FRAMING IS THE WRONG MODEL, the same way the widening-SITE count was the wrong model for Group A. Sizing as asked: our callee-saved order is s0<-p78 (10/39/7692), s1<-p72 arg0 (8/70/3428), s2<-p73 arg1 (8/89/2696), s3<-p118 (3/14/2142), s4<-p77 big_size (4/52/1538), s5<-p74 var_s5 (2/120/166). Target puts big_size in s0. For our p77 to reach s0 it must outrank p78 at 7692, a 5.0x lift, and the formula gives exactly two routes, BOTH blocked by the algorithm's real structure: nrefs 4 -> 14 at livelen 52 (floor_log2(n)*n must exceed 40; n=13 gives 7500, still short, n=14 gives 8076), or livelen 52 -> <=10 with nrefs 4, which would require the DMA block to sit adjacent to the rounding block. Neither is a hirahira-style +1 gap. BUT THE TARGET ASM SAYS THE INVERSION IS NOT REAL: target line 123 is `bne $s0, $a0` inside the push loop, so target's s0 holds the LOOP value there, exactly as ours does - target does not keep big_size in s0. What target actually does is compute big_size into s0 TRANSIENTLY, copy it out through v1 into s4 (`move v1,s0` / `sll v0,v1,0x4` / `move s4,v1` at indices 53-58), and then reuse s0 for the loop. We compute big_size straight into s4 and use s0 for the loop throughout. So Group B's residual is a MISSING TRANSIENT COPY CHAIN around big_size - a CSE/structure question - not an allocno-priority tie, and no amount of priority lifting addresses it. The round-9 `big_stage` probe (staging big_size through a second variable) was the right instinct but the wrong shape and scored 30. RECOMMENDATION: bank at 30. Group A and C are closed, the frame and instruction count are exact, and the remaining 30 is one well-identified structural question that the priority ladder provably cannot reach.

sessions.lever: ra_solver round: model validates 23/23. big_size needs pri > 7692 vs its current 1538 (a 5x lift) to take $s0, because the $s queue is handed out in strict descending priority order; perturb finds NO vector (133 atoms + greedy), including the conflict/pref/birth atoms. Group B is also not purely naming - the clamp region is misordered.
sessions.note: Ran the ra_solver pipeline on the banked score-30 candidate. Extraction + simulate validate 23/23 against the dump (free regression check). The callee-save queue, in allocation order, is: 78 -> $s0 (nrefs 10, livelen 39, pri 7692), 72 -> $s1 (8/70, 3428), 73 -> $s2 (8/89, 2696), 118 -> $s3 (3/14, 2142), 77 -> $s4 (4/52, pri 1538) = big_size, 74 -> $s5 (2/120, 166). Target holds big_size in $s0. The $s registers are handed out in STRICT DESCENDING PRIORITY ORDER, so big_size would have to be FIRST in this queue: pri > 7692 against its current 1538, a 5x lift. At livelen 52 that needs nrefs about 8; at nrefs 4 it needs livelen <= 10. perturb.py with spec {77:16}, 133 single atoms plus greedy: NO sufficient vector - no refs, live-length, conflict, preference or birth-order atom reaches it, because the required lift is far outside single-atom range. This settles the r8 note's suggestion that the priority framing is the wrong model and that the solver's conflict/pref/birth atoms are the other models: for CE0C the callee-save assignment IS a pure priority queue, and the non-priority atoms do not help either. SECOND FINDING: Group B is not purely register naming. 51 of 143 lines differ and from about line 26 the clamp region is MISORDERED, not just renamed - target has sh v1,4(s1) at line 27 where ours has it at 30, and target loads lh a1,6(s1) where we emit lhu v1,6(s1) plus a separate lh a2,6(s1). So Group B is a shape problem in the clamps plus the callee-save queue, not the roughly 30-insn rename the earlier note described. THIRD FINDING (new sweep): accumulator type. s16 v1_tmp gives 51 differing lines, the same as the banked u16; s16 a0_tmp and both-s16 are worse at 53. The u16 choice costs nothing measurable but is also not what produces target's lh at the clamp read. RECOMMENDED ORDER for whoever resumes: fix the clamp shape first (target loads lh a1,4(s1) once and uses a1 for both the bltz and the slt, threading move v1,a1 into the branch delay slot; we emit a load, a load-delay nop and a move with the slt operands swapped - the coord = (v1_tmp = arg0->x) double-assign is the likely cause). That will re-price the queue, so re-derive the model afterwards rather than working the current priorities. src/display.c reverted.

root_cause: Three independent causes. (A) The frame is 16 bytes short because cc1 allocates half as many phantom locals temps as the original did (vars 16 vs 32) - not a spill, not a dead array, and not reachable by declaring locals. (B) Register allocation in the clamp and multiply blocks plus three extra/missing moves. (C) One superfluous argument load at the func_8007DC9C call.
next_avenues: GROUP B (the whole residual, 30) is NOT a priority tie - target computes big_size into s0 transiently, copies it out through v1 into s4, then reuses s0 for the push loop; we compute it straight into s4 and hold s0 for the loop. The open question is what source shape makes cc1 emit that transient + copy chain (indices 53-58: move v1,s0 / sll v0,v1,0x4 / move s4,v1). Round-9's big_stage probe was the right instinct, wrong shape.

The x-clamp block restructured under the r8 frame fix and has NOT been re-derived; it currently emits `lhu v1,4(s1)` where target has `lh`. Prefer `s16 v1_tmp` (same score 30, sign-extending load) as the base for that re-derivation. That block may be the larger share of the 30.
